_note: 英語版ページの「日本語名の意味」。確かなものだけ書く。parts は [日本語, ローマ字, 意味]

bulbasaur.text: Its name is literally “mysterious seed” – fitting for the bulb on its back.

ivysaur.text: The seed has sprouted, so the name changes from “seed” to “plant”.

venusaur.text: The last stage of the line: the plant finally becomes a “mysterious flower”.

charmander.text: A plain and perfect description: a “fire lizard”.

charmeleon.text: The Japanese name is just the English word “lizard” written in katakana.

charizard.text: “Lizard” plus the “-don” ending heard in dinosaur names like iguanodon.

squirtle.text: Zenigame is a real Japanese word for a baby turtle. It literally means “coin turtle”, because the shell looks like an old coin.

butterfree.text: From the English word “butterfly”, the same as in English.

beedrill.text: Named after the spears on its arms.

pidgey.text: Poppo is the sound a pigeon makes in Japanese – the same sound as in the children’s song “Hato poppo”.

rattata.text: A “little rat”. Its evolution is simply ラッタ, “rat”.

raticate.text: Just “rat” – the little ko (子) is dropped once it grows up.

spearow.text: A “demon sparrow”, because of its fierce temper.

ekans.text: Like its English name (snake backwards), the Japanese name is “boa” read backwards.

arbok.text: “Kobra” spelled backwards – the same trick as its English name.

pikachu.text: Pika is the Japanese sound of something flashing or sparkling, and chū is the squeak of a mouse.

sandslash.text: Sand plus pangolin, the scaly animal it is based on.

clefable.text: The English word “pixie”, a small fairy.

vulpix.text: Roku is six (its six tails) and kon is the sound a fox makes in Japanese.

ninetales.text: Six tails become nine: kyū is nine. It is based on the nine-tailed fox of Japanese legend.

jigglypuff.text: Purin is the Japanese word for custard pudding – soft, round and wobbly.

gloom.text: A “smelly flower” – which is also a pun on kusa (grass).

vileplume.text: Named after Rafflesia, the giant flower that smells of rotten meat.

parasect.text: A parasite and an insect in one name.

venomoth.text: From the morpho, a large and colourful butterfly.

dugtrio.text: Three Diglett digging together: a trio.

meowth.text: Nyā is how a cat says “meow” in Japanese.

persian.text: Named after the Persian cat breed.

golduck.text: The little duck grows into a golden duck.

growlithe.text: From “guard” or “guardian” – it is a loyal guard dog.

arcanine.text: From “windy”, because it runs as fast as the wind.

poliwag.text: Nyoro-nyoro is the Japanese sound of something wriggling, like a tadpole’s tail.

kadabra.text: Based on Uri Geller, the famous spoon-bender. He later sued over the name, and Kadabra disappeared from Pokémon cards for about twenty years.

alakazam.text: Named after the escape artist Harry Houdini.

machop.text: Wanryoku means physical strength in your arms.

machoke.text: The strength level goes up: gōriki is “mighty strength”.

machamp.text: Kairiki means superhuman strength. The three names show the strength going up step by step.

bellsprout.text: “Still a bud” – it has not bloomed yet.

victreebel.text: From utsubo-kazura, the Japanese name for the pitcher plant that traps insects.

tentacool.text: An “eyed jellyfish”, after the red gems that look like eyes.

geodude.text: Ishitsubute means a stone thrown at someone.

graveler.text: Goro-goro is the Japanese sound of something heavy rolling.

rapidash.text: From “gallop”, the fastest way a horse runs.

slowpoke.text: Yadokari is a hermit crab (it ends up carrying a Shellder) and don means dull or slow.

magnemite.text: From the English word “coil”, as in an electric coil.

magneton.text: A “rare coil” – three Coil joined together.

farfetchd.text: From the Japanese saying “kamo ga negi wo shotte kuru” – a duck turning up carrying its own leek, ready for the pot. It means something conveniently falling into your lap.

dodrio.text: A dodo with three heads: a trio.

dewgong.text: Named after the dugong, a sea mammal.

grimer.text: Betobeto is the Japanese word for something sticky and gooey.

muk.text: Even more sticky goo than Grimer.

gastly.text: From “ghost”. Its evolution’s Japanese name is exactly ゴースト (ghost).

haunter.text: The English word “ghost”, written in katakana.

gengar.text: From Doppelgänger, a ghostly double of a living person.

onix.text: Iwa means rock – fitting for a giant rock snake.

hypno.text: From “sleeper” – it puts others to sleep.

voltorb.text: Biri-biri is the Japanese sound of an electric shock, and tama means ball.

electrode.text: A “round mine” – a land mine that explodes.

exeggcute.text: Tama means ball and also comes from tamago (egg). It is doubled because it is a group of eggs.

cubone.text: Karakara is the sound of something dry and hollow rattling.

marowak.text: Garagara is a louder rattle, and also the Japanese word for a baby’s rattle toy.

hitmonlee.text: Named after Tadashi Sawamura, a famous Japanese kickboxer – it is the kicking Pokémon.

hitmonchan.text: Named after Hiroyuki Ebihara, a Japanese boxing champion – it is the punching Pokémon.

lickitung.text: Bero is a casual Japanese word for tongue.

weezing.text: “More poison gas” – two Koffing joined together.

rhyhorn.text: Sai is the Japanese word for rhinoceros.

rhydon.text: Rhino plus the “-don” of dinosaur names.

chansey.text: From the English word “lucky” – it is said to bring happiness.

horsea.text: From tatsu-no-otoshigo, the Japanese word for seahorse, which literally means “dragon’s child”.

goldeen.text: Named after the Tosakin, a fancy goldfish breed from Kōchi with a fan-shaped tail.

mr-mime.text: From “barrier”, after the invisible walls it builds by miming.

jynx.text: From rouge, the French word for red lipstick.

tauros.text: From kentauros, the centaur of Greek myth, and tauros, Greek for bull.

magikarp.text: The “carp king” – a big name for the weakest Pokémon.

ditto.text: From metamorphosis, the act of changing shape.

flareon.text: From “booster”, as in a rocket booster.

porygon.text: From polygon – it is made of computer graphics.

omanyte.text: From the ammonite, a real fossil shellfish.

kabuto.text: Kabuto is a samurai helmet, and kabutogani is the Japanese name for the horseshoe crab it is based on.

aerodactyl.text: From the pteranodon, a flying reptile.

articuno.text: Simply “freezer”. The three legendary birds are named fire, thunder and freezer in Japanese.

dragonite.text: A “sea dragon” – the Pokédex says it lives in the sea.

mewtwo.text: The same as in English: Mew number two.

bayleef.text: The bay leaf, a herb used in cooking.

typhlosion.text: Bakufū is the blast of wind from an explosion.

treecko.text: A “tree gecko”. A real spider was named after its English name in 2021.

grovyle.text: Usually explained as jungle plus reptile.

torchic.text: Shamo is a breed of fighting rooster.

mudkip.text: Water plus mutsugorō, a mudskipper fish found on Japanese mud flats.

grotle.text: A turtle carrying a small grove.

torterra.text: A tortoise as big as the ground itself.

monferno.text: The fire gets stronger: mōka is a raging fire.

infernape.text: Gōka is the fire of hell – the three names show the flame growing.

tepig.text: Poka-poka means nice and warm, and buta is pig.

oshawott.text: Maru is an old ending for boys’ names, often given to young samurai.

dewott.text: It fights with two scalchops, like a samurai with two swords.

rowlet.text: Wood plus fukurō, the Japanese word for owl.

popplio.text: A sea lion playing with a ball.

grookey.text: Nori means getting into the rhythm – it is a drumming monkey.

sobble.text: Meso-meso is the Japanese sound of someone quietly crying.
